title: SST data of January 2021 to September 2026 did not support the AMOC slowing forecast of Ditlevsen and Ditlevsen (2023): the refitted tipping year moved later in six HadISST1 and ERSSTv5 versions
abstract: We did an out-of-sample test of the AMOC collapse forecast of Ditlevsen and Ditlevsen (2023, DD23). DD23 fitted a ramped fold model to the monthly subpolar gyre SST minus two times the global mean SST in HadISST1 for 1870-2020. We fitted the same model to 1870-2020 only and scored the 69 new months from January 2021 to September 2026 against the model and against a no-slowing Ornstein-Uhlenbeck null with the same mean shape. We used six fingerprint versions from HadISST1 and ERSSTv5. Our primary HadISST1 fit replicates DD23 (ramp start 1922, tipping year 2055.7). In the new months, the log likelihood ratio of the DD23 model against the null was -1.19 (expected +0.33 if the model is true; 5.9% of model simulations were this low), and it was negative in 5 of 6 versions. After we added the new months, the tipping year moved later in all six versions: from 2055.7 to 2066.4 in the primary version, later than 97% of refits of data simulated from the DD23 model. The shifts were +4 to +16 years in HadISST1 and +31 and +51 years in ERSSTv5. The fingerprint stopped falling because the subpolar gyre warmed in 2021-2024. The low month-to-month persistence of HadISST1 after 2020 (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.54) is not in ERSSTv5 (0.77) or OISST (0.69), so part of the HadISST1 shift is a product effect. The new data do not reject the model at a strict level: if the DD23 model is true, 10:1 evidence is expected in half of the cases by about 2031, and if the null is true, by about 2038. The fitted model also puts 83% of noise-induced collapses before its deterministic tipping year (median 2045.6). Limitations: a short test period, an approximate replication without the DD23 penalty, one choice of null model, and no test of whether the fingerprint represents the AMOC.
